To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the group III metabotropic receptor mGlu7 is expressed on a ventral mesencehlon human neural stem/progencitor cell (hNPSC) line, that selective activation of this receptor induces an anti-prolificative effect and that tonic exposure of differentiating cultures to this agonist induces astrocyte differentiation.
selective activation of mGlu7 receptors inhibits cellular proliferation and promotes differentiation of VM-derived hNSPCs.
the group III mGlur agonist L-AP4 selectively activates mGlu7 receptors to inhibit cellular proliferation and promote astrocyte differentiation in ventral mesencepahlon-derived hNSPC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel targets for cell replacement therapies for neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease (PD).
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for Parkinson's disease (PD) and related disorders of the basal ganglia, such as progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP).
the development of a novel strategy for the modulation of hNSPC proliferation and differentiation using the mGluR subtype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mGlu7 agonism can be used to control the proliferation of hNSPC and promote their astrocytic differentiation.
the mGluR7 subtype is a novel and promising target to control the proliferation and differentiation potential of hNSPC.
the mGluR7 receptor provides a new opportunity for the manipulation of human neural stem/progencitor cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mGlu7 activation has the ability to selectively reduce the number of proliferating cells and promote astrocyte fate in VM hNSPC.
the mGlu receptor subtype, mGlu7, is expressed in human ventral mesencephioc-derived neural stem/progenitors cells.

the mGluR7 receptor is involved in the proliferation of undifferentiated human neural stem/prognitor cells derived from the ventral mesencehpalon and the mGluRs 4, 7, 8 receptors are involved in the differentiation of these cells into glia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mGlu7 activation can be used to promote astrocyte differentiation and inhibit proliferation of hNSPC.
mGlu7 receptors are expressed by human ventral mesencechelon derived hNSPCs, and that activation of mGlu7 can reduce proliferation and increase astrocytic differentiation of these cells.

the mGluR7 subtype of metabotropic glutamatergic receptors is expressed on human neural stem cells and that activation of this receptor subtype can modulate the proliferation and differentiation potential of these cells.
